transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2026-03-03 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Eva (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood CSM), Jared (CTO, Northbridge), Priya (Security Lead), Maya (PM)

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll keep this to about an hour. i'm Samir, AE on the account, Eva our solutions engineer will walk through the console and retention controls. lena from success is here to help with next steps. quick round robin?
[00:12] Jared: Jared here, CTO. i'm interested in how you handle PII and retention — we have strict cardholder data policies and need to keep trfc logs minimal.
[00:20] Priya: yeah hi priya, security lead. SOC2, encryption at rest, and KMS integration are key for us; also need proof of deletion.
[00:28] Maya: maya - product. i want to understand how toggles affect analytics and debugging.
[00:33] Eva: cool, thanks. i'll do a live console walkthrough. quick qualifier — are you currently using any hosted LLM vendors or self-host?
[00:40] Jared: we have a mix — some OpenAI for prototyping and an internal self-hosted Llama cluster for sensitive flows. we're evaluating for production; want to know how Redwood compares on controls and cost.
[00:51] Samir: good, that maps to what others asked. i'll flag that dedicated/private options are available if you need VPC or on-prem. for this session we'll demo the hosted Console controls and API no-store flags then discuss Dedicated/Private later.
[01:05] Eva: starting share - Console: project -> Data Controls. first toggle is "Request Storage". default in hosted is on, which stores request/response for debugging and evals. you can set per-project TTL (30d, 90d, custom) or turn storage off entirely.
[01:22] Eva: when storage is off, we still keep minimal audit metadata for billing and routing but not the input text or output. this is exposed via the API flag store=false on request payloads. note: if you turn storage off you lose automatic transcripts for the request in the Console.
[01:37] Priya: when you say minimal audit metadata - what fields do you keep? do you keep any user identifiers or IPs?
[01:43] Eva: good q — we keep non-PII metrics: token counts, model used, timestamp, and anonymized route ids. we don't retain IPs by default in hosted — for Dedicated/Private we can mirror customer audit requirements.
[01:57] Maya: is there a way to redact only specific fields? for example mask the PAN in JSON payloads but keep other fields.
[02:03] Eva: yes, field-level redaction. Console allows you to define redaction rules: regex patterns, JSON paths, and pre-built PII detectors (card numbers, ssn, email). you can set action: mask, remove, or pseudonymize. regex can be applied at ingest or during logging.
[02:19] Jared: regex + PII detectors sound useful. how reliable are the detectors? false positive risk?
[02:25] Eva: detectors are ML-backed with tuned thresholds; you can tune sensitivity per project. we also support a manual allowlist/denylist. there are occasional false positives — we showed earlier that the system surfaces confidence score in the logs so you can review before bulk delete.
[02:40] Samir: just to add - we provide a CLI tool and API to run a bulk scrub on historical stored data if you enable storage for pilot then later need to purge. we'll provide attestations for deletion in enterprise contracts.
[02:52] Priya: and KMS? how does key management work for stored artifacts and logs?
[02:57] Eva: Redwood supports both managed keys and customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM in Dedicated and Private deployments. for hosted, you can request CMEK for encryption at rest in certain tiers. keys are used for stored request blobs and also for backup snapshots.
[03:13] Maya: what about embeddings or vector DB storage — do those obey the retention toggles?
[03:18] Eva: good catch — embeddings are stored in a separate index; retention is configurable independently. you can opt to disable embedding storage or set a different TTL. note: some features like semantic search and rerank may require embeddings stored; we have an on-the-fly embed option that caches transiently to avoid long-term storage.
[03:33] Jared: can we control these via API for dynamic decisions? e.g., store=false for high-risk requests and store=true for others?
[03:40] Eva: yes - store flag can be passed per-request. we also support per-route policies (e.g., all payments routes default to no-store). policies can be tied to JWT claims or headers to make routing decisions.
[03:51] Priya: audit logs and immutability — we need tamper-evident logs for compliance. do you provide append-only audit trails?
[03:58] Eva: audit logs are available; for Dedicated/Private we support forwarding to your SIEM via syslog/Kafka and can store hashes of events in an append-only ledger. for hosted, we provide export of audit events and time-stamped signatures, but for absolute immutability we recommend Dedicated with your SIEM.
[04:16] Samir: let's switch to a quick demo of the UI redaction rule editor.
[04:20] [screen share: redaction rule page]
[04:24] Eva: here is a redaction rule: name = "Payment PAN mask". pattern=\"\\b(?:4[0-9]{12}(?:[0-9]{3})?)\\b\" (visa approx). action=mask with last4 preserved. you can test against sample payloads in the console.
[04:39] Maya: nice, can we do custom serializers so downstream logs show tokenized or hashed values?
[04:45] Eva: yes, for pseudonymize we generate a deterministic salt-hash per project so downstream analytics can do joins without exposing raw PII.
[04:53] Jared: are there implications for caching/KV cache if we pseudonymize? does it break dedupe and batching?
[04:59] Eva: depends — caching is keyed on the preprocessed prompt. if pseudonymization is applied before caching then similar inputs map to same key. if you mask or remove fields you may reduce cache hit rate. Optimize recommendations will flag that in the cost/latency report.
[05:15] Priya: what about GDPR/CCPA right-to-be-forgotten?
[05:18] Eva: we have a delete-by-identifier API. you submit the identifier and our backend finds and deletes stored artifacts per TTL rules; for Hosted there is a deletion SLA for pilot customers in enterprise tiers. For Dedicated, customer retains full control. We also provide export to satisfy data portability requests.
[05:35] Samir: quick note - request storage off is compatible with some features but disables built-in evals and automatic transcripts, and it impacts the ability for Redwood to debug incidents unless you provide a repro. we'll document the trade-offs.
[05:48] Maya: can we do partial redact then store for a limited window to allow debugging, then auto-delete?
[05:53] Eva: yes, set a short TTL + redaction rule. many customers do a 7-day retention with pan masked then auto-delete.
[06:02] [06:02] Jared: switching to API example - Eva, can you show the request payload example for no-store?
[06:07] Eva: sure - sample in docs: POST /v1/generate with headers Authorization + Project-ID; body includes input and "store": false, "redaction": {"mode":"mask", "rules":[...]} . i will paste the exact snippet after the call, but main idea is store flag is first-class.
[06:22] Priya: if someone forgets store=false in client, can we enforce policies server-side?
[06:27] Eva: yes - route policies and per-project defaults can enforce store=false for routes with sensitive indicators. you can also use token scopes that disallow storage.
[06:35] Samir: let's talk about logs forwarded to SIEM and retention retention TTLs.
[06:39] Eva: you can configure retention to be X days, and configure export to S3/Kafka. export can redact fields before forwarding. for PCI-level workloads most customers use Dedicated plus forwarding to their PCI-scoped SIEM and enable HSM keys.
[06:52] Maya: what's the pilot experience look like? if we run a 30-day pilot with 5M tokens/month how would storage default and price?
[06:59] Samir: we'll send a tailored pilot pricing doc. short version: hosted pay-as-you-go with optional add-on for extended retention; Dedicated gives predictable commit pricing. we'll follow up with exact numbers.
[07:12] [07:12] Priya: any certifications? you mentioned SOC2 earlier - do you have ISO?
[07:16] Samir: we are SOC2 Type II. ISO in progress. we'll send the whitepaper and latest audit artifacts.
[07:24] Eva: moving on to live demo of Optimize tab - this is relevant because retention choices affect unit economics.
[07:30] [screen share: Optimize > Caching Recommendations]
[07:33] Eva: Optimize detects repeated prefixes and suggests caching or prefix-hash to reduce tokens sent to model. it also flags when redaction is lowering cache hits and shows a projected cost delta.
[07:43] Maya: can Optimize automatically create redaction-safe cache keys?
[07:46] Eva: we have an option to use hashed placeholders for PII in the canonicalized prompt used for caching. that's a safe-mode to retain cache effectiveness while not exposing raw PII in keys.
[07:57] Jared: from infra perspective, we need network diagrams for Dedicated and Private, and port requirements for SIEM forwarding.
[08:03] Samir: we'll include an architecture diagram in the follow-up; Eva will lead the deep dive.
[08:09] Priya: about attestations - how do we prove deletion? is there a cert or log we can pull?
[08:15] Eva: we emit deletion events and can provide a time-stamped audit trail of deletions. for Dedicated we can sign the events with your KMS key. for hosted we'll provide signed attestations from Redwood.
[08:29] Jared: any limitations on redaction performance? like latency overhead?
[08:33] Eva: redaction at ingest adds ~5-20ms depending on complexity of regex/ML detectors. pseudonymization and hashing are negligible. bulk scrubs may take longer depending on dataset size.
[08:45] [08:45] Maya: are there sample policies/templates for mapping product routes to retention settings?
[08:49] Eva: yes we ship policy templates (payments, support chats, analytics) you can import and tweak.
[08:56] Priya: if we go Dedicated, is there an option to keep certain logs only on-prem?
[09:01] Eva: yes - for Private/On-prem you control storage. we can provide agent-based connectors to push only meta events.
[09:08] Samir: quick recap of trade-offs: storage on = easier debugging, evals, and some Optimize features; storage off = stronger privacy compliance but less observability; redaction reduces risk but may reduce cache. Dedicated/Private unlocks KMS, SIEM forwarding, and stronger immutability guarantees.
[09:26] Jared: ok, that's helpful. next steps?
[09:29] Lena: i'll summarize: we'll send SOC2 + KMS docs, sample network diagram and pilot pricing. Eva will schedule a technical deep dive for VPC/KMS and provide sample retention configs. Jared will share estimated volumes and any internal compliance checklist.
[09:40] Maya: can you also share a short clip showing the retention toggle and redaction test? would be useful for our stakeholders.
[09:45] Samir: yes, we'll include a short clip in the follow-up.
[09:50] [minor crosstalk as people confirm next steps]
[09:54] Priya: one last q — if we set store=false but still want to collect redacted traces for anomaly detection, is that possible?
[09:59] Eva: yes, you can configure a pipeline to keep only signal-level metrics (no raw tokens) and forward redacted traces. that's common for fraud detection.
[10:07] Jared: thanks everyone.
[10:09] Samir: thanks for your time; we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule.

End of transcript

Notes on transcription quality: some product names transcribed inconsistently (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes "K V cache"). occasional filler words and overlapping talk.
